sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four statements or pairs of ½ mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or arrange in sequence).

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Food can get contaminated by flies. (ii) A crowded place can be a source of disease-causing germs. (iii) All children need not be given full vaccination. (iv) Drinking water should be boiled for 10 minutes to make it germ-free.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) True. (iii) False – all children should be fully vaccinated. (iv) True.

questions.q: Match the communicable disease with its incubation period: (I) Tuberculosis (II) Pertussis (III) Influenza (IV) Hepatitis; (a) 1–3 days (b) 4–6 days (c) 20–35 days (d) 7–12 days.

Fill in the blanks: To make ORS at home, mix ______ teaspoons of sugar and ______ teaspoon of salt in 1 litre of clean drinking water; ORS packet contents are mixed with ______ only; infants are fed with a ______ and not a bottle.
questions.note: April 2024 asked: to make ORS at home mix ______ and ______ to 1 litre clean drinking water (sugar and salt).

questions.q: State True or False: (i) HIV/AIDS spreads through shaking hands. (ii) An HIV-infected person may not have AIDS. (iii) Infected needles can spread HIV. (iv) There is a vaccine for HIV/AIDS.
questions.answer: (i) False. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) False – there is no vaccine or cure.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Which four precautions would you adopt to prevent communicable diseases?
questions.answer: Keep food and water covered and boil drinking water; wash hands before eating and cooking and after using the toilet; keep the house and surroundings clean with covered drains and wire mesh on windows; get children completely vaccinated; avoid crowds in an epidemic; keep the patient's things separate (any four).

questions.q: List any four myths regarding the spread of HIV/AIDS.
questions.answer: HIV does not spread by shaking hands, kissing on the cheek, using the same toilet seat, standing close to or sitting with the infected person, sneezing or coughing, sharing cups, glasses and plates, or through food and water.

or.q: Write four causes of increase in lifestyle diseases.
or.answer: Junk and processed food; less physical activity (use of vehicles and machines); smoking and drinking; stress; overeating and obesity; replacement of milk and fresh fruits by soft drinks and packed foods.

questions.q: Write any four reasons of transmission of HIV/AIDS. Expand HIV.
questions.answer: HIV stands for Human Immuno Deficiency Virus. It spreads by sexual contact with an infected person, by infected blood or body fluids (transfusion), by infected needles, and from an infected mother to her child during pregnancy or at birth.

questions.q: Name any four diseases related to life style.
questions.answer: Obesity, diabetes, hypertension (high blood pressure), heart disease (any four; also stroke and some cancers).

questions.q: Your neighbour is often sick. Suggest four ways to remain disease-free.
questions.answer: Eat a balanced diet; exercise regularly; keep personal and surrounding hygiene; drink boiled or safe water and keep food covered; get vaccinated; avoid smoking and alcohol; manage stress with yoga.

questions.q: What is meant by incubation period? Give one example.
questions.answer: It is the gap between the entry of germs and the appearance of the symptoms of the disease. For example, typhoid symptoms may appear 14–21 days after the infected food was eaten; the person is a carrier meanwhile.

questions.q: How is ORS prepared at home when a packet is not available?
questions.answer: Add 8 teaspoons of sugar and 1 teaspoon of salt to 1 litre of clean drinking water, dissolve and stir well.

questions.q: Distinguish between communicable and life style diseases (two points).
questions.answer: Communicable diseases are caused by germs and spread from one person to another through food, water, air, contact or insects; life style diseases do not spread, they arise from faulty eating and living habits. Communicable diseases are usually short-term (acute) and curable, while life style diseases are chronic and can only be controlled.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Write any six reasons for the increase in life style diseases.
questions.answer: (1) Fast food and junk food replacing nutritious balanced meals. (2) More processed and packed food, rich in sugar, fat and salt. (3) Soft drinks replacing milk. (4) Use of bus or car even for short distances. (5) Machines reducing physical labour. (6) Smoking and drinking among young people. (7) Stress. (8) Overweight and obesity.

questions.q: Shazia ate food exposed to flies and dust at a fair; the next day she had vomiting, diarrhoea and leg cramps. Name the disease and write three steps to manage her.
questions.answer: These are symptoms of cholera, spread through contaminated food and water. Management: give plenty of fluids and ORS to prevent dehydration; give boiled water and fresh, easily digestible food; take her to a doctor for tests and medicine; keep her clean and rested.

questions.q: Explain how communicable diseases spread, giving one example for each mode.
questions.answer: Food and water – typhoid, cholera, hepatitis through contaminated food and water. Air – influenza and mumps by sneezing or coughing. Contact – direct (common cold, diphtheria, measles) or indirect through shared towel, cup or comb. Insects – malaria and dengue by mosquito bite; flies carry germs to food.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Suggest five ways by which life style diseases can be prevented.
questions.answer: (1) Take regular exercise such as walking, yoga, cycling. (2) Use stairs instead of the lift. (3) Eat a balanced diet at proper times and do not overeat. (4) Avoid processed and packaged foods and eat whole grains, millets and 400–500 g fruits and vegetables daily. (5) Drink plenty of water. (6) Practise yoga or meditation to avoid stress. (7) Keep away from smoking and alcohol; watch less TV and do outdoor activities.

questions.q: Give the mode of spread, any three symptoms and the care of a patient of typhoid or tuberculosis.
questions.answer: Typhoid: spreads through contaminated food and water; symptoms – severe headache, fever with low pulse, dry white-coated tongue (appear after 14–21 days); care – blood tests, prescribed medicines, boiled water and fresh easily digestible food, rest. Tuberculosis: spreads through air; symptoms – persistent cough, loss of weight and appetite, excessive weakness, chest pain; care – hygienic conditions, calcium-rich diet, regular medicines for one year, covering the mouth while coughing and isolation.
